newsitem.title: USA: Goodyear, union say contract talks resume.
newsitem.headline: Goodyear, union say contract talks resume.

text.p: Goodyear Tire & Rubber Co. and the United Steelworkers of America resumed contract talks Monday, one day after nearly 13,000 union rubber workers walked out over an impasse in contract negotiations.
Spokesmen for the company and the union said negotiations resumed Monday morning in Cincinnati but that only a portion of the full negotiating committees were taking part.
The rubber workers, members of the United Steelworkers, walked out at one minute after midnight Sunday in the first strike at Goodyear in 21 years.

The striking workers are employed at Goodyear plants in Akron, Marysville, and St. Marys, Ohio; Gadsden, Ala.; Lincoln, Neb.; Topeka, Kansas; Danville, Va.; Union City, Tenn.; and Sun Prairie, Wis., Brown said.

They walked out after two months of negotiations failed to resolve disputes standing in the way of a proposed three-year contract. Goodyear was selected by the union April 1 as its target to set the pattern for 1997 bargaining with the industry.
Issues in the dispute include job security, shifting work to outside contractors, contract revisions and certain partnership arrangements, said the union.
The strike was the first to hit Goodyear since a 140-day- long work stoppage that paralysed the tire industry in 1976.
Goodyear employs 91,000 people at dozens of plants around the world. The stock of the company, the largest U.S. tiremaker, was off 1/4 at 52-1/4.
